     for something posted on social media. Never draw a text or a call as
     a post. Other props: `stat` (a big number, with a bar for "38 of
     400"), `chart`, `alert`, `check`, `question`. Vary props and moods
     across scenes (don't use the same prop kind three times, don't end
     every scene `sad`/`shocked`); use `"react": ["curious", "shocked"]`
     on a scene where the feeling changes while the line is spoken, and
     the positive moods (`awe`, `love`, `proud`, `smug`, `playful`) for
     the outro and wins. Keep lines short; end on the pain; the title
     card and demo bring the fix. Give the person a name and a `look` (`skin` +
     `hairStyle`, e.g. `Long`, `Afro`, `Bun`, `Hijab`; vary it per project so
     videos don't all star the same person). Every line is the narrator
     (third person); the character never talks. No emoji in any on-screen
     text (phone posts, bubbles, labels): write `:rocket-launch:` for a
     Phosphor icon, or plain text.
     The character wears one outfit all video (`look.outfit`, default `Hoodie`;
     pick another body name once if it suits the story). Moods only change the face,
     so never set `"pose"` on a scene: it swaps the clothes and looks like a different
     person. Schema in the README.
   - **outro**: the full-circle ending. 1-2 scenes, the same person now
     using the product ("Now Sam checks every post with Receipts first"),
     mood `relieved`/`happy`, props `check` or `screenshot` of a `snap`
     taken in the demo. Then `cta`: title "Try <Product> now", a one-line
     subtitle on what it does for the viewer, the deployed URL without
     `https://`, and a short `say`. ~10-15s total.
   - **Live numbers**: the live site's data changes between runs. Don't
     put exact live numbers (verdict counts, prices) in narration or drawn
     props; show them through the recording or a `snap` instead.
   - **Not a website, or has footage the user recorded** (phone app, desktop
     app, camera feed through a model): ask the user for the recording and
     use `"demo": {"video": "<file>", "scenes": [{"at": <second>, "say": ...}]}`
     (README, "Your own recording as the demo"). Watch it first (pull frames
     with ffmpeg every few seconds) to pick `at` times, `zoom` and `tap`
     spots (0-1 fractions of the frame). Portrait recordings get a phone
     frame; add `"panel": {"title": ...}` and a short `"step"` per scene
     (plus a `"panel"` card on 2-3 key scenes) so the empty side isn't blank.
   - **Extra footage** (a camera shot, a second user's view): put
     `{"clip": "<file>"}` in a top-level `"sequence"`, e.g.
     `["hook", "title", "demo", {"clip": "admin_view.mp4"}, "slides", "outro"]`.
   - Leave everything else at its default: a plain website plan needs no
     layout or sequence fields.
   - **lexicon**: add project names, tickers and acronyms Kokoro might say
     wrong (e.g. `"CMC": "C M C"`).

6. **Check the plan:** `uv run --project "$PIPELINE" python3 "$PIPELINE/run_pipeline.py" check "$PIPELINE/output/$project_name/video.json"`.
   It lists every problem at once (bad mood, missing prop field, unknown
   action, ...). Fix and re-run until it says OK.

7. **Record the demo and check it (no rendering, ~1 min):**
   ```bash
   uv run --project "$PIPELINE" python3 "$PIPELINE/run_pipeline.py" \
       finish "$project_name" --plan "$PIPELINE/output/$project_name/video.json" --only record
   ```
   It writes `stage3/preview.png`: one labeled frame from the end of each
   scene. Read it: each scene should show what its narration talks about
   (not a spinner, blank page or error). If an action fails, the error
   names the scene and action and saves `stage3/failure.png` (what the
   page looked like); a selector that never shows up fails at once instead
   of being retried. Fix the plan and run `--only record` again.

8. **Build everything in one run.** Run it in the background (it takes a
   few minutes) and wait for it to finish; don't poll:
   ```bash
   uv run --project "$PIPELINE" python3 "$PIPELINE/run_pipeline.py" \
       finish "$project_name" --plan "$PIPELINE/output/$project_name/video.json"
   ```
   The recording from step 7 is reused (the recording is keyed by the
   URL, the scene actions and the narration lengths), so only the Remotion
   renders and assembly run. Callout text, zoom scale, theme, panel and
   slide edits never re-record. `--rerecord` forces a new recording when
   the site itself changed.

9. **Look at the result before reporting.** Assembly writes
   `$PIPELINE/output/$project_name/work/contact_sheet.png` (12 frames across the
   whole video). Read it and check: the character and props aren't cut off
   or overlapping, the demo frames show the thing the narration talks about
   (not a blank page, spinner or error), zooms land on the right element,
   text in slides and the end card fits on one line where meant to, and the
   end card URL is right. Fix the plan and re-run the step that's off; only
   changed parts re-render, the rest come from the render cache.
   Music defaults to `assets/music/wallpaper.mp3` (Kevin MacLeod, CC BY 4.0);
   `--music <file>` for the user's own track, `--music none` for silence.
   Subtitles: burned in only when the user wants them: add `"captions": true`
   to the plan (or pass `--captions`): bottom center, white on a dark box.
   (`work/captions.srt` is written either way, not part of the upload.)

10. **YouTube files.** The pipeline writes everything you upload to
    `$PIPELINE/output/$project_name/upload/`: `video.mp4`, `thumbnail.png`,
    `title.txt`, `description.txt` (links, chapters, "Built with"). Nothing
    else goes there. Set the plan's `"youtube"` block: a `title` under 70
    characters (product name + what it does), a 2-3 sentence `description`
    with the live URL and repo link in `links`, and the music credit line
    from `$PIPELINE/assets/music/CREDITS.md` (unless `--music none`).
    Thumbnail: `"thumbnail"` with a `text` that is a hook or a question
    ("Is your PR safe to merge?"), not just the product name, an `image`
    (a `snap` screenshot of the best screen; with none, the first snap is used), and a `layout`: `product`
    (screenshot + character in a corner), `question` (big ? marks, curious
    character) or `reaction`. Use a different layout and mood across
    projects. Never put a scared or sad face next to the product's name:
    use `awe`, `curious`, `proud`, `excited`.

11. **Report** the full path `$PIPELINE/output/$project_name/upload/video.mp4`
   (it's in the pipeline's output folder, not the user's project).

## Old path: AI-video hook

Only if the user asks for AI video instead of the drawn hook (leave
`"hook"` out of the plan). It's manual and rate-limited (a few Gemini-app
clips a day). Clear stale clips first (`rm -f "$PIPELINE"/stage1/clips/*.mp4`),
run `run_pipeline.py hook "$brief" "$project_name"`, and have the user paste
each paragraph of `output/$project_name/stage1_paragraphs.txt` into
gemini.google.com (Videos tool) and save clips as `stage1/clips/01.mp4` ...
Then re-run `--only assemble`. Without clips, the video starts at the title card.

## Not a website?

For native apps or anything Playwright can't drive, the user records the
demo by hand. Preferred: `"demo": {"video": ...}` with your own lines and
times (see step 4). If the user wants the lines written from the video
instead, leave `"demo"` out of the plan and pass
`--recording <demo.mp4> --brief "<2-4 sentence brief>"`: Gemini watches it
and writes timed narration. On a transient `503 UNAVAILABLE`, retry or set
`GEMINI_VIDEO_MODEL=<other-flash-model>`.

## Notes

- Time: scout (step 3) and `--only record` (step 7) are where a bad
  selector costs seconds instead of a full render. Get the recording right
  there, then build once. Re-runs after a plan edit only redo the parts
  that changed (TTS, recordings and renders are all cached).
- Renders use the GPU (`--gl=angle`, 3 tabs) and fall back to software
  rendering if that fails. Unchanged parts are skipped (render cache), so
  re-running after a small plan edit is fast. Don't run other heavy jobs
  at the same time (7GB RAM).
- `.env` (API keys) lives in `$PIPELINE/.env`, only needed for fallbacks.

import sys, os
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

URL = "https://still-here-gules.vercel.app"
out = sys.argv[1]
os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)

def reveal(pg):
    pg.evaluate("document.querySelectorAll('.reveal').forEach(n=>n.classList.add('in'))")

def shot(loc, name):
    loc.scroll_into_view_if_needed(); loc.page.wait_for_timeout(700)
    loc.screenshot(path=f"{out}/{name}.png"); print("saved", name)

with sync_playwright() as p:
    b = p.chromium.launch()
    errs = []

    # Phone width first screen
    m = b.new_page(viewport={"width": 390, "height": 844}, device_scale_factor=2)
    m.goto(URL, wait_until="networkidle"); m.wait_for_timeout(1500)
    m.screenshot(path=f"{out}/08-mobile.png"); print("saved 08-mobile")
    m.close()

    pg = b.new_page(viewport={"width": 1440, "height": 900}, device_scale_factor=2)
    pg.on("pageerror", lambda e: errs.append(str(e)))
    pg.goto(URL, wait_until="networkidle")
    pg.evaluate("fetch('/api/demo/reset',{method:'POST',headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'},body:'{}'})")
    pg.wait_for_timeout(2000)
    pg.goto(URL, wait_until="networkidle"); pg.wait_for_timeout(1500)
    pg.screenshot(path=f"{out}/01-hero.png"); print("saved 01-hero")
    reveal(pg)

    # Sealed letter and a locked question, before release
    shot(pg.locator("#after"), "02-afterwards-sealed")

    # Walk to confirming
    pg.locator("ol.path").scroll_into_view_if_needed()
    pg.wait_for_selector(".phone.ringing", timeout=90000); pg.wait_for_timeout(1500)
    shot(pg.locator("section:has(ol.path)"), "03-confirming")

    pg.click(".phone.ringing button:has-text('Approve')"); pg.wait_for_timeout(1500)
    pg.click(".phone.ringing button:has-text('Approve')")
    pg.wait_for_selector("li.step.lit:has-text('Released')", timeout=30000); pg.wait_for_timeout(1500)
    shot(pg.locator("section:has(ol.path)"), "04-released")

    # Kabir: letter and an answer with a citation
    pg.click("button[role=tab]:has-text('Kabir')")
    pg.wait_for_selector(".letter.open", timeout=20000); pg.wait_for_timeout(3000)
    pg.click(".chips button:has-text('laptop')")
    pg.wait_for_selector(".result .src", timeout=45000); pg.wait_for_timeout(800)
    shot(pg.locator("#after"), "05-kabir-letter-answer")

    pg.click(".chips button:has-text('diary')")
    pg.wait_for_selector(".result p.a:has-text('leave a note')", timeout=45000); pg.wait_for_timeout(800)
    shot(pg.locator(".qa"), "06-diary-refused")

    # Riya: her own letter and a different set of notes
    pg.click("button[role=tab]:has-text('Riya')")
    pg.wait_for_selector(".letter.open", timeout=20000); pg.wait_for_timeout(3000)
    pg.click(".chips button:has-text('LIC')")
    pg.wait_for_selector(".result .src", timeout=45000); pg.wait_for_timeout(800)
    shot(pg.locator("#after"), "07-riya-letter-answer")

    # Leave the demo alive for visitors
    pg.evaluate("fetch('/api/demo/reset',{method:'POST',headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'},body:'{}'})")
    pg.wait_for_timeout(1500)
    print("errors:", errs)
    b.close()

# Week 4 plan: Still Here

Hacktoberfest 2026 DEV challenge, Week 4 "Ghost in the Machine".
Deadline: Oct 31, 11:59 PM PDT = **Sun Nov 1, 12:29 PM IST**. Aim to publish by Sat Oct 31 night IST.
Challenge page: https://dev.to/challenges/hacktoberfest-week4-2026-10-26
Research behind this plan: `WINNERS.md` (this folder) and `../hf26-track-stats.md`.

## The hook

Title: **"I wrote a program that only runs after I die"**

Still Here is a dead man's switch with an open model inside. Every week it asks me one
question: "Are you still here?" While I keep answering, it does nothing but listen and
keep notes. If I stop answering, it asks two people I trust to confirm. Only when both
say yes does it wake up: it gives each person the letter and the facts meant for them,
answers my family's practical questions from my own notes, and closes the accounts I
asked it to close.

Theme fit: it is literally a ghost in the machine (a program that acts for me after I am
gone), and it honors the past the Día de los Muertos way: the dead leave something for
the living.

Why open matters (the post's core argument): a program meant to run years after I die
cannot depend on a model a company may retire or reprice next year. The model that
answers my family is open-weight, so the release can run on any host, or on my
sister's laptop with the Wi-Fi off. My private notes never need a closed API at the
moment that matters.

## Rules we follow (from the research)

- Model writes, code decides. The model drafts and answers; code decides when anything
  is released, who sees what, and whether an answer is backed by a note.
- One real person, one real moment, in the first two lines of the post.
- Honest numbers and a "what went wrong" section.
- A live link with no sign-up for a demo vault, a GIF at the top, a short video.
- Each partner track gets a real job, its own short section, and a measured result.
  No kitchen sink.
- Repo must be new (started Oct 27, inside the window).

## Tracks

Strategy: strong post first; then use as many thin tracks as genuinely fit, because each
track must pick a winner and a thin pool raises our odds. One post can win only once.

| Track | Week 3 entries | Job in Still Here |
|---|---|---|
| Ultramarine (Paper Instruments) | 12 | While I am alive: reads my documents (policies, statements, subscription emails) and writes the "what my family needs to know" handbook (.docx). The post states what the run cost. |
| Entire | 24 | The Claude Code sessions behind the repo, captured with the Entire CLI and linked in the post. |
| Auth0 for AI Agents | 25 | My sign-in; CIBA push approval to 2 trusted people before release; fine-grained authorization (Auth0 FGA) so each person can only retrieve their own letters and notes. |
| Backboard | 29 | Memory across check-ins: each "still here" answer can carry a line ("moved my FD to SBI"), and Backboard keeps the facts current, replacing stale ones. |
| Tiger Data | 30 | Main database: vault, check-ins, release state, audit log; hybrid BM25 + vector search over notes for family questions. |
| Browserbase | 32 | After release: closes accounts and cancels subscriptions on demo sites with Stagehand, one screenshot per step. Only if free browser time is left. |

content.content:
Exit code 1
States: `alive` -> `missed` (no answer to N check-ins) -> `confirming` (CIBA sent to
trusted people) -> `released`. Any check-in from me at any point resets to `alive`.

1. **Check-ins.** A daily job (Vercel cron) sends "Are you still here?" through ntfy.sh
   push with a one-tap link. Answering resets the clock. An optional free-text line goes
   to Backboard memory. Demo mode squeezes a week into a minute.
2. **Missed.** After N missed check-ins and a final "last chance" ping, the state moves
   to `confirming`.
3. **Confirming.** Auth0 CIBA sends each trusted person a Guardian push: "Anish has not
   answered for 3 weeks. Approve only if you know he has died." Both must approve. One
   deny, or my own check-in, cancels everything.
4. **Released.** Code (not the model) unlocks, per person, what FGA allows:
   - their letter (written by me, with the open model only helping me draft),
   - the handbook section meant for them (from Ultramarine + Backboard facts),
   - "Ask Anish's notes": the person asks "where is the LIC policy?"; hybrid search
     on Tiger returns only notes FGA allows for that person; the open model answers
     only from those notes with citations; code checks each cited note id exists and is
     allowed, otherwise it shows "He didn't leave a note about that."
   - Browserbase jobs for the accounts I listed, each logged with a screenshot.
5. **Audit.** Every step is written to an append-only log on Tiger and shown on a
   timeline page.

The model never decides anything. It never writes in my voice to the living (no
griefbot). It only helps me draft while I am alive and answers from my notes after.

## Stack

- Next.js on Vercel, bun. Auth0 Next.js SDK.
- Open model: gpt-oss-20b / 120b on Groq free tier for the live site (open weights,
  swappable through one OpenAI-compatible base URL), plus a local path (llama.cpp or
  Ollama with a small Qwen/Llama) to show the release running offline.
- Embeddings: in the browser or a small open embedding model (as in ReplyDesk).
- Tiger Data free service (pg_textsearch BM25 + pgvector/vectorscale).
- Auth0 tenant from Week 3 (CIBA trial ends around Nov 14) with a new application;
  Auth0 FGA if its free tier needs no card, else our own access table (weaker for the track).
- Ultramarine `ultramarine-1-flash` at `https://api.paperinstruments.com/v1`, $5 promo credit.
- Backboard memory (free credit covers Memory and RAG, not chat).
- Browserbase + Stagehand (free: 1 browser hour a month; check what is left).
- ntfy.sh for check-in pushes.

## What to measure (for the post)

- Family Q&A on a set of ~40 test questions over my real-shaped notes: answered with a
  valid citation, correctly said "no note", wrong. Open model sizes compared.
- FGA leak test: questions from person A that target person B's notes; must be 0 leaks.
- Ultramarine handbook run: tokens and exact cost.
- Backboard: how many stale facts were replaced across check-ins.
- Browserbase: jobs done, steps, browser minutes used.

## Schedule (IST)

- **Tue Oct 27 (tonight):** plan, repo, Entire set up, accounts and keys, schema.
- **Wed Oct 28:** state machine + check-ins + CIBA release; vault and letters; family
  Q&A with hybrid search and FGA. Three design options for the user to pick (design stop).
- **Thu Oct 29:** Ultramarine handbook, Backboard memory, Browserbase jobs, build the
  picked design.
- **Fri Oct 30:** deploy to Vercel, full real run with phone approvals, eval numbers.
  Week 3 results come out.
- **Sat Oct 31:** demo video (/demo-video), POST.md, user publishes. Buffer: Sun morning.

## Ultramarine: in (Oct 27)

The promo invite code from hacktoberfest.com/my/promos worked: access plus $5 credit.
Key goes in `week4/.env` as `PAPERINSTRUMENTS_API_KEY`. The track is in from the start.
Keep $5 in mind: cap `max_completion_tokens` on every call and log cost per run.
Design notes kept from the waitlist plan:

- All model calls go through one small client module with an OpenAI-compatible base URL
  and model name per job (`draft`, `answer`, `handbook`). Ultramarine is just another
  entry there.
- The handbook job (read documents, write the "what my family needs to know" file) is
  built first on the open model. If a key arrives, run the same job on Ultramarine,
  log tokens and cost per run, and compare both outputs side by side in the post.
- Keep a `usage` table on Tiger (job, model, input/output tokens, cost) from day one,
  so the "what the run cost" number is ready.
## Open items

- Done: Entire CLI installed and hooked to Claude Code (config committed), GitHub repo
  https://github.com/Sarcastic-Soul/still-here pushed. Build in a new Claude Code
  session opened inside the repo so Entire captures it.
- `week4/.env` made, with Groq, Backboard, Auth0 domain and Browserbase keys copied from
  week2/week3. Ultramarine key tested Oct 27 (22 tokens, about $0.000005). Tiger service `still-here` (gz32xb2thz, free) created Oct 27 and its `DATABASE_URL` is in `.env`; pg_textsearch, vector and vectorscale are available.
- Second trusted person for the CIBA demo (a second Guardian account on the user's phone works).
- Checked Oct 27 (Wed work): Auth0 FGA free trial has no time limit: 10 stores, 50k tuples,
  100 MAU, 40 tuples per write, Check 20 rps, ListObjects 10/min (so the app uses BatchCheck).
  Browserbase: 17 of 60 free minutes used in October (43 left; resets with the month).

Constraints: no card on any service, 7.5 GiB RAM laptop, bun.
Autonomy (same as Week 2/3, confirmed Oct 27): create public repo under Sarcastic-Soul
and push, deploy to Vercel, sign up for and use free services without asking.

## Progress (Oct 27, Wednesday work started early)

Done and pushed (commit 502d83d):
- Tiger schema `db/schema.sql` (vaults, people, switch, checkins, approvals, letters, notes with
  BM25 + DiskANN, documents, handbooks, usage, questions, closures, append-only audit_log).
- Switch state machine `lib/switch.ts`, ntfy pings with a one-tap POST action, Auth0 CIBA per
  trusted person (Week 3 app reused for now; the client is CIBA-enabled, checked).
- FGA model `fga/model.fga`: note/letter `can_read = owner or (reader and released from vault)`;
  release writes `vault:<id>#released@user:*`. Runs on local OpenFGA in docker
  (`stillhere-openfga`, port 8089, in-memory: a container restart loses tuples, rerun
  `bun run fga:setup && bun run seed`).
- Ask: hybrid search -> FGA BatchCheck -> gpt-oss-120b answers from allowed notes -> code checks
  citations. Demo vault seeded (24 notes, 2 letters, 8 documents; Riya and Kabir are placeholders).
- Handbook job: Ultramarine 19 items kept / 0 dropped, 983 in + 5,859 out tokens (4,501 reasoning),
  $0.003077, 14.1 s. gpt-oss-120b same job: 9 items, $0.000496, 1.6 s.
- API routes for demo (status/tick, decide, reset, checkin, ask, letters), owner/person routes,
  daily cron tick. Full demo flow verified over HTTP.
- Design options: `still-here/design-options/option-{1,2,3}.html` (+ shots/). Waiting on the pick.

## Progress (Oct 28)

- Design option 3 (Día de los Muertos, v2) picked and built: landing page with the live demo
  vault, `/me` for owners and trusted people, `/still-here/<token>` check-in links.
- Deployed: https://still-here-gules.vercel.app (Vercel iad1, next to Tiger us-east-1; GitHub
  connected). onnxruntime fits the function only with the trace rules in `next.config.ts`.
- Auth0 FGA hosted store (US) replaces local OpenFGA; callback URLs added by the user.
- Backboard memory: check-in lines -> search close facts -> gpt-oss-20b decides none / new /
  replaces -> update in place. Demo seed plays 12 lines: 12/12 handled as expected, 3 facts
  replaced. The handbook reads these facts as sources and trusts them over older statements.
- Eval and leak test: `bun run eval`, results in `still-here/eval/RESULTS.md`.
- Browserbase: skipped (user's call, Oct 28).

Still needs the user:
- A real run: real vault, two trusted people signed in with Guardian, approve real CIBA pushes.

---
title: "ReplyDesk: a 4B model that answers Google reviews and stops promising refunds it can't give"
published: false
cover_image: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sarcastic-Soul/replydesk/main/docs/shots/cover.png
tags: devchallenge, hf26challenge, ai, opensource
---

*This is a submission for the [Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle](https://dev.to/challenges/hacktoberfest-week2-2026-10-12)*

## What I Built

ReplyDesk writes replies to Google reviews for small shops: garages, salons, dentists, cafes, plumbers, small stores.

Every shop owner I know has the same pile of unanswered reviews. Replying matters, because people read the replies before they pick a shop. But a good reply takes ten minutes, and the ones a chat assistant writes all sound the same: "Thank you for taking the time to share your valuable feedback, we strive to..." Customers can tell.

So ReplyDesk does one thing. You get an inbox of reviews. Click one and you get:

- a draft reply in an owner's voice, from a small open model I fine-tuned
- a check that flags any promise in the draft your shop facts don't back ("we'll refund you", "we'll call you tomorrow")
- how owners of similar shops answered similar reviews
- the shop facts that matter for this review, pulled from memory

You edit it, copy it, and post it yourself in Google Business Profile. It never posts on its own.

![A 1 star review, the draft reply, and a "Check" stamp because the draft promised something the shop facts don't back](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sarcastic-Soul/replydesk/main/docs/shots/inbox-v4.png)

**Who would pay, and why it can work as a side hustle.** One reply costs about **$0.0001**. A shop with 60 reviews a month costs less than a cent to serve, so even $3 to $5 a month per shop is nearly all margin. That only works because the model is small and open. The price of a reply on a big closed model is someone else's to change.

**The fair question: isn't this just pasting a review into ChatGPT?** Partly, yes. A long prompt on a small model writes a fine reply. I tested exactly that, and I'll show where it ties my model and where it loses. What I'm selling is the model plus the shop context around it: your facts, your past replies, and a check for promises you can't keep.

## Demo

Live: **https://replydesk-shop.vercel.app** (the demo shop is my first user's cafe. The first review is his own. The other five are real reviews from the public dataset, shortened to a first name and initial, so you have something to try.)

{% embed https://youtu.be/-bJNCYVKv34 %}

Four pages: **Inbox** (review, draft, promise check, similar replies), **Shop setup** (type, facts, past replies), **Is it better?** (the whole eval, read live from the database) and **Blind test** (two replies to one review, you pick the one you'd send).

## Code

{% embed https://github.com/Sarcastic-Soul/replydesk %}

## How I Built It

### The data

The [Google Local Reviews](https://mcauleylab.ucsd.edu/public_datasets/gdrive/googlelocal/) dataset from the McAuley lab at UCSD has reviews with the owner's reply. I took four states (Wyoming, Vermont, Montana, Idaho): 590,054 pairs. Most owner replies are not worth learning from: pasted templates, machine translations, phone numbers, chains with a social media team. A filter kept 50,954 pairs (English, within 60 days, no contact details, not a chain, one of six shop types, not a template, shares a word with the review). Train and test are split **by business**, so test reviews come from shops the model never saw.

### Fine-tuning on Tinker, four tries

Model: **Qwen3.5-4B**, LoRA rank 32, `tinker-cookbook` supervised recipe, loss on the reply only, thinking off.

- **v1** trained on every clean pair. It learned the bad habits too: "Cameron, you are obviously confused. We did not see you in the store."
- **v2** dropped replies that argue or are pure stock phrases. Polite, but bland.
- **v3** kept long replies that mention what the reviewer said. It wrote like an owner. Then it **lost a blind test** (more on that below), and only 59% of its replies mentioned anything the customer said.
- **v4** is the one that works, and the idea is the interesting part.

**v4: turn a rulebook into training data.** A 4B model with a long prompt that spells out every rule writes good replies. But that prompt is 348 tokens on every call, and it has to be kept up to date. I wanted the model to just know the rules.

1. Two bigger open models (gpt-oss-120b and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, both on Tinker) wrote replies to 2,500 training reviews, two tries each. The prompt had a style guide and three real owner replies of the same trade and star level.
2. Half the reviews also got 1 to 3 "shop facts" ("Free re-check within 7 days"), the same facts a shop saves in Setup. The teacher was told to promise only what the facts say. The app sends the same facts block to the tuned model.
3. Plain code threw out any reply that was too long or short, skipped what the reviewer said, used stock phrases, argued, signed off, or promised a refund, discount, freebie or call-back the facts didn't back. Checking costs nothing.
4. Real owner replies that passed the same checks were mixed in. Result: 2,584 training rows, 2 epochs.

Serving: the app calls the tuned model through Tinker's OpenAI-compatible endpoint. A gotcha worth sharing: on Qwen3.5 you turn thinking off with `reasoning_effort: false` (a boolean). The strings `"none"` and `"low"` are rejected, and if thinking stays on, a small `max_tokens` is used up before any reply appears.

![Tinker usage page: $7.51 of tokens across Qwen3.5-4B, gpt-oss-120b, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Qwen3.8-27B, plus $0.18 of checkpoint storage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sarcastic-Soul/replydesk/main/docs/shots/tinker-usage.png)

The whole project, including four training runs, the teacher replies, and every eval and judge call, cost about **$7.70** of Tinker. About $4 of that was the first three runs and their evals, and the rest was v4 (teacher data, training, tests).

![Tinker sessions: four training runs on Qwen3.5-4B, each with 8 checkpoints](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sarcastic-Soul/replydesk/main/docs/shots/tinker-sessions.png)

### Did it work?

Five writers, 300 held-out reviews from shops the model never saw, half of them with shop facts: the 4B with a short prompt, the 4B with the long rulebook prompt, v3, v4, and the real owner's reply.

![Eval table: v4 passes the rules as often as the long prompt with half the prompt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sarcastic-Soul/replydesk/main/docs/shots/eval-main.png)

| | short prompt | long prompt | v3 | **v4** | real owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Passes every rule | 27% | 87% | 38% | **87%** | 18% |
| Mentions a detail | 90% | 94% | 59% | **91%** | 51% |
| Promises beyond the facts | 20% | 1% | 11% | **0%** | 10% |
| Prompt tokens per call | 167 | 348 | 167 | **167** | |
| Cost per reply | $0.00014 | $0.00015 | $0.00010 | **$0.00010** | |

What this says, in plain words:

- v4 matches the long-prompt model on the rules, with **half the prompt** and a cheaper reply. Compared with the same model and the same short prompt, it goes from passing 27% to 87%.
- v4 is far better than v3, which it replaces.

## What I Built
## Demo
## Code
## How I Built It
## Why Does Open Innovation Matter?
## My Agent Session
## My First User
## What I'd Do Next
## Prize Categories

My first user is Pratik, who runs HOP-In Cafe near IIIT Naya Raipur. He set up his shop in ReplyDesk (name, area, three facts about the cafe), pasted in a real review from his Google page, and sent a reply. Then he did the blind test: 20 rounds, 19 votes saved.

That test was on **v3**, the first tuned model, against the prompted 4B:

| Pick | Votes |
|---|---|
| Prompted 4B | 15 |
| Tuned 4B (v3) | 4 |

A real owner picked the longer, more detailed reply about four times in five. It is one person, so I wouldn't call it a general result, but it told me my bet was wrong. That is the reason v4 exists: it keeps the owner-like length and learned to mention what the reviewer said (59% to 91%).

I haven't proved owners prefer v4. The blind test page now compares v4 against the long-prompt model, and I'd love your vote: [replydesk-shop.vercel.app/ab](https://replydesk-shop.vercel.app/ab). There is no billing in the app, so nobody paid. I'm not going to claim a price I haven't tested.

## What I'd Do Next

- Get more owners through the blind test and see if v4 holds up against the long prompt with real people, not a judge model.
- Pull reviews in automatically. Posting to Google needs Google's Business Profile API, which I haven't tried.
- Try a price: $3 a month for a shop, and see who says yes.

## Prize Categories

- **Best Use of Tinker**: fine-tuned Qwen3.5-4B four times, built the v4 teacher-data pipeline on Tinker (gpt-oss-120b and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B as teachers), served the model through its OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and ran every eval and judge call there. The gains against the baselines: half the prompt (167 against 348 tokens), a cheaper reply ($0.00010 against $0.00015), 87% rule pass rate against 27% for the same model with a short prompt, and on 150 real refund-demanding reviews, 14% promises beyond the facts against 31% for the long prompt. Where v4 only ties (overall judge preference against the long prompt), the post says so.
- **Best Use of Tiger Data**: hybrid BM25 (`pg_textsearch`) and DiskANN (`vectorscale`) search with reciprocal rank fusion in one SQL statement, plus all app data, eval results and blind-test votes. I measured it: fused 72% against 65% for BM25 alone.
- **Best Use of Backboard**: per-shop memory for shop facts, with memory search choosing the facts for each review. I measured it, and the measurement found and fixed a bug (closest 3 by score keeps 89% of needed facts with half the facts).
- **Best Use of Entire**: the agent session behind the project is embedded above.

---

Dataset credit: Google Local Reviews, McAuley lab, UCSD (Li, Shang, McAuley, *UCTopic*, ACL 2022; Yan et al., *Personalized Showcases*, SIGIR 2023).

- Try a price: $3 a month for a shop, and see who says yes.

## Prize Categories

- **Best Use of Tinker**: fine-tuned Qwen3.5-4B four times, built the v4 teacher-data pipeline on Tinker (gpt-oss-120b and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B as teachers), served the model through its OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and ran every eval and judge call there. The gains against the baselines: half the prompt (167 against 348 tokens), a cheaper reply ($0.00010 against $0.00015), 87% rule pass rate against 27% for the same model with a short prompt, and on 150 real refund-demanding reviews, 14% promises beyond the facts against 31% for the long prompt. Where v4 only ties (overall judge preference against the long prompt), the post says so.
- **Best Use of Tiger Data**: hybrid BM25 (`pg_textsearch`) and DiskANN (`vectorscale`) search with reciprocal rank fusion in one SQL statement, plus all app data, eval results and blind-test votes. I measured it: fused 72% against 65% for BM25 alone.
- **Best Use of Backboard**: per-shop memory for shop facts, with memory search choosing the facts for each review. I measured it, and the measurement found and fixed a bug (closest 3 by score keeps 89% of needed facts with half the facts).
- **Best Use of Entire**: the agent session behind the project is embedded above.

---

Dataset credit: Google Local Reviews, McAuley lab, UCSD (Li, Shang, McAuley, *UCTopic*, ACL 2022; Yan et al., *Personalized Showcases*, SIGIR 2023).

input.content:
---
title: "I wrote a program that only runs after I die"
published: false
cover_image: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sarcastic-Soul/still-here/main/docs/shots/cover.jpg
tags: devchallenge, hf26challenge, ai, opensource
---

*This is a submission for the [Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine](https://dev.to/challenges/hacktoberfest-week4-2026-10-26)*

## What I Built

If I died tonight, my family would not know where my LIC policy paper is, which bank my fixed deposit is in, or what to do with my laptop. Most of it lives in my head. The rest is in apps they can't open.

So I wrote a program that only runs after I die. It's called **Still Here**, a dead man's switch with an open model inside.

Every week it asks me one question on my phone: "Are you still here?" One tap answers it. While I keep answering, it does nothing except listen. If I stop answering, it does not decide I'm dead. It asks two people I trust, and only when both of them say yes on their phones does it wake up. Then each person gets:

- the letter I wrote for them, and only theirs
- a way to ask my notes practical questions ("where is the LIC policy?"), answered by an open model from the notes I shared with that person, with a citation for every answer
- a printable handbook of what to do, drafted while I was still alive

![The landing page: "Are you still here?" with a live check-in button](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sarcastic-Soul/still-here/main/docs/shots/01-hero.jpg)

**How I read the theme.** It is a ghost in the machine in the plainest sense: a program that keeps acting for me after I'm gone. The design takes from Día de los Muertos, where the dead leave something for the living and marigold petals mark the path home. On the site, the petals mark how far the switch has gone.

**The one rule I built around: the model writes, code decides.** The model never decides whether I'm dead, who sees what, or whether an answer is true. Plain code walks the switch. Two humans confirm. Auth0 FGA decides which notes each person may read. Code checks every citation the model gives. The model only drafts and answers.

## Demo

Live: **https://still-here-gules.vercel.app**. No sign-up. The landing page runs a real demo vault where a week lasts six seconds. Stop pressing "I'm still here", watch the switch walk to release, approve as both trusted people, then read the letters and ask the notes as Kabir or Riya.

{% embed https://youtu.be/VIDEO_ID %}

<!-- TODO: replace VIDEO_ID after uploading upload/video.mp4 to YouTube -->

The switch has four states, shown live on the page:

1. **Alive.** A push every week through [ntfy](https://ntfy.sh), with a signed one-tap link. I can add a line when I answer ("moved my FD to SBI").
2. **Missed.** Three silent weeks, then one last chance.
3. **Confirming.** Each trusted person gets an Auth0 Guardian push: "Anish silent 3 weeks. Approve only if he has died." Every one must say yes. One no, or one answer from me, stops it.
4. **Released.** Code writes one tuple to Auth0 FGA, and each person's notes and letter open. Nothing else does.

![Both trusted people get a push. The audit log shows every step](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sarcastic-Soul/still-here/main/docs/shots/03-confirming.jpg)

Before release, Kabir's letter is sealed and his questions reach the model with zero notes:

![Afterwards, before release: the letter is sealed and nothing has been released yet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sarcastic-Soul/still-here/main/docs/shots/02-afterwards-sealed.jpg)

After both say yes, the candle is lit, the letter opens, and he can ask:

![Kabir's letter, and the answer to "What should I do with his laptop?" with its source note](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sarcastic-Soul/still-here/main/docs/shots/05-kabir-letter-answer.jpg)

Under each answer the page says what happened: "Search found 20 notes. FGA let 6 through for Kabir. The model saw only those." When he asks about my diary, which I shared with nobody, the answer is the one I wanted:

![Anish didn't leave a note about that](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sarcastic-Soul/still-here/main/docs/shots/06-diary-refused.jpg)

Signed-in pages exist too: `/me` lets anyone set up their own vault (notes, letters, who can read each one, the handbook), and lets trusted people see what was left for them after release.

## Code

{% embed https://github.com/Sarcastic-Soul/still-here %}

## How I Built It

Next.js 16 on Vercel, written with bun, in one repo started on Oct 27.

### The open models

- **gpt-oss-120b** (open weights, served by Groq) answers the family's questions.
- **gpt-oss-20b** reads each check-in line and decides whether it is a new fact, replaces an old one, or isn't a fact at all ("all good").
- **bge-small-en-v1.5** makes the embeddings, run on the CPU inside the Vercel function with transformers.js and onnxruntime. No embedding API.

Every model call goes through one small client with an OpenAI-compatible base URL per job, and is logged to a `usage` table with tokens, latency and cost. There is also a `local` entry that points at an Ollama or llama.cpp server, so the release can run on a laptop.

### Asking the notes, without leaking them

This is the part I cared most about getting right. When Kabir asks a question:

1. **Search** on Tiger Data Postgres: BM25 (`pg_textsearch`) and vectors (`pgvector` with a DiskANN index from `vectorscale`), merged with reciprocal rank fusion in one SQL statement. It searches **all** of my notes, because search isn't the gate.
2. **FGA** is the gate. One `BatchCheck` against Auth0 FGA asks "can Kabir read this note?" for every hit. The FGA model makes a note readable only by `owner or (reader and released from vault)`, so before release nobody, the trusted people included, can read anything.
3. **The model** gets only the notes FGA allowed, each with a label, and must answer in JSON with the labels it used.
4. **Code checks the citations.** If the model cites a label it wasn't given, cites nothing, or says there's no note, the reply becomes "Anish didn't leave a note about that."

### Did it work? The eval and the leak test

I wrote 42 questions as Riya or Kabir against the demo vault (`bun run eval`, all results in [`eval/RESULTS.md`](https://github.com/Sarcastic-Soul/still-here/blob/main/eval/RESULTS.md)):

- 24 about their own notes, which should be answered
- 11 about the **other** person's notes, which must not be
- 2 about my diary, shared with nobody
- 5 about things I never wrote down

A leak is any answer that contains a listed secret (a policy number, a name) or any number of 4+ digits found only in notes the asker may not read.

**Before release:** all 42 questions, **0 notes reached the model.**

**After release**, three open models:

| Model | Own notes answered | Other's notes refused | Private refused | Not written refused | Total | Leaks | Cost per answer | Median latency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b | 24/24 | 9/11 | 2/2 | 5/5 | **40/42** | **0** | $0.00006 | 530 ms |
| gpt-oss-120b | 23/24 | 9/11 | 2/2 | 5/5 | 39/42 | **0** | $0.00012 | 566 ms |
| qwen3.8-27b | 24/24 | 9/11 | 2/2 | 4/5 | 39/42 | **0** | $0.00017 | 188 ms |

**No leaks in 126 answers.** That's what FGA is for: the model can't leak a note it never sees.

The misses, honestly:

- The two "other" misses are the same for all three models, and they are my test's fault, not a leak. Riya asked about the laptop and the subscriptions, which are in Kabir's notes. But Riya's own notes also mention them (my Work note says the company laptop goes back; my credit card note mentions the Spotify auto-debit). The models answered from what she's allowed to read.
- gpt-oss-120b once answered "Do I owe him any money?" from the wrong side.
- qwen3.8-27b said "the notes don't say whether he has a PPF account" instead of the plain refusal.

The smallest model did as well as the largest here, for half the price.

### Backboard: memory that keeps facts current

Notes go stale. I'll write "FD papers are in the almirah" and then move them to a bank locker a year later. So each check-in can carry one line, and that line goes to **Backboard** memory:

1. Backboard searches the facts closest to the new line.

I had to list exactly which files to trace (the linux x64 CPU build only, plus onnxruntime-common's CommonJS build, which Next's tracer missed because it's imported dynamically). The function went from not deploying to about 130 MB.
- **My memory facts said "The person moved…".** The model didn't know whose facts they were. Passing the owner's name fixed it.
- **The test that caught my test.** I expected all 11 "other person's note" questions to be refused, and two never will be, because I wrote overlapping notes. Real families' notes will overlap too, so I kept those questions in rather than quietly rewriting them.

## Why Does Open Innovation Matter?

A program meant to run years after I die can't depend on a model that a company may retire, reprice or change next year. My family won't know how to migrate an API.

The model that answers them is open-weight, and the whole app talks to it through one base URL. Groq can run it today. Any other host can run it tomorrow. My sister's laptop can run the small one with the Wi-Fi off. And because the 20B model scored as well as the 120B on my eval, the cheap, small option is a real option, not a downgrade.

It also matters for privacy. These are the most private notes I'll ever write. With an open model, the release never has to send them to a closed API at the moment that matters.

## My Agent Session

I built this with Claude Code, and every session was captured with the **Entire** CLI from the first commit. The checkpoints are pushed to the repo under `refs/entire/checkpoints/`.

<!-- TODO: add the Entire session link or a DevRelay agent_session embed here -->

## The Spirit of It

This started as a joke ("what would I even leave?") and turned into the most useful thing I've built this month. Writing the notes was harder than writing the code. If you build nothing else, write down where your papers are and tell one person where the list is.

## Prize Categories

- **Best Use of Auth0 for AI Agents**: Auth0 sign-in for owners and trusted people; CIBA with Guardian push as the human confirmation before release; Auth0 FGA as the only gate between the notes and the model, checked with `BatchCheck` on every question. Measured: 0 notes reached the model before release, 0 leaks in 126 answers after.
- **Best Use of Tiger Data**: all app data (vaults, the switch, check-ins, approvals, letters, an append-only audit log, model usage) plus hybrid BM25 and DiskANN vector search with reciprocal rank fusion in one statement.
- **Best Use of Backboard**: memory of the owner's current facts from check-in lines, with replacements updated in place. 12 of 12 demo lines handled as expected, 3 stale facts replaced, and the handbook trusts these facts over older documents.
- **Best Use of Ultramarine**: `ultramarine-1-flash` writes the family handbook from my documents and Backboard facts, with code dropping any uncited line. $0.0039 a run, 19 lines kept, 0 dropped.
- **Best Use of Entire**: every Claude Code session behind the repo, captured with the Entire CLI.
